analysis:
Examined the memory-accounting and reclaim changes. EngineProcessMemoryOwner.swift (head 11-21, 60-73) adds an optional onRefusal callback. On insufficientCapacity it computes ledger.capacityShortfall and signals, then rethrows the same refusal. It does not change the fail-closed charge semantics, and the callback is non-blocking and runs under the owner lock. The callee, ledger.capacityShortfall, is outside the supplied evidence and is assumed to be a scalar read that cannot re-enter the owner lock or deadlock.

GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift adds signalsEngineRefusals, an idle-gated cache sweep (sweepWindow/idleClearCache), releaseRetained, and directChargeRefusalSignal. The env toggle DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP=0 is local-operator-controlled and affects only availability and performance, not confidentiality or authorization. The idle clear uses serviceBudget.performIfIdle after a stream synchronize. The clear is allowed only when no fault is retained, via the existing isReclaimAllowed hook. The retained-fault and unretired-closing-transaction guard stays intact, so reclaim still does not refund owner claims. The new releaseRetained closure and CBv2RetainedKVSegments.requestRelease are unseen. Dropping retained free KV segments relates to T-028 (residual GPU data) and could in principle reduce residual data, which would be a benefit rather than a regression. Host-zeroed backing is reportedly returned to the OS.

MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift (head 963-964, 1074) only passes onRefusal: budget.directChargeRefusalSignal() into MiMoV26ManagedMediaReservation. The initializer change is in an unseen file. The retire path shown in the head text is unchanged context. Shortfall signals carry only byte counts and no prompt content.

I found no regression against T-041, T-028, T-029 or the trust boundaries. The cache-storage and encryption controls are untouched. Remaining questions: ProcessMemoryLedger.capacityShortfall locking, KVPoolReclaimer's new sweepWindow and releaseRetained semantics, and the rate-limit/DoS properties of repeated refusal-triggered reclaims. These are in unseen files, so a low-priority deeper check is reasonable.
